decisions.reason: The 2020–2021 collapse in air travel likely left the app below aspiration and drew down slack. Still, contactless processing is in demand as traffic recovers, and the app costs little to maintain, so management is more likely to keep it while searching than to drop it outright.

PassBoard was a flagship launch that builds on the firm's core passenger-screening know-how, and recovering airports need efficient, low-contact processing, so its results are attributed to the pandemic rather than the product and it is retained.

Self-service check-in fits the post-COVID push for touchless, cost-saving passenger handling at the firm's airport and airline clients, so despite weak recent results it is kept to capture recovering demand.
